html:
Novosibirsk is the largest city in Siberia, founded in 1893 where the Trans-Siberian Railway was to cross the Ob River. It was first named Novonikolayevsk, after the soon-to-be Tsar Nicholas II, and renamed Novosibirsk, "new Siberia", in 1925.

The railway bridge made it a hub where grain, coal from the Kuznetsk basin and, later, the Turkestan-Siberia line all met. It grew from a workers' settlement to the third largest city in Russia in about a century, one of the fastest rises of any city in the world. In the Second World War whole factories and theatres were moved here from the west, out of reach of the German army.

In 1957 the Soviet Academy of Sciences began building Akademgorodok, a science town in the forest south of the city, which became one of the main research centres of the Soviet Union. The city now has over 1.6 million people. It took the lead in Siberia from older towns like Tobolsk, which the railway passed by.
